rv.q: Matthew Warchus’s beautifully controlled and intelligent production is all shifting nuance and finely calibrated detail...
The joy of the evening lies in watching Fiennes at the height of his powers and relishing a play that offers one of the most searing self-portraits in drama.
The Master Builder at The Old Vic not only does justice to Ibsen but is theatre at its best: bold, relevant, brilliantly acted and compelling.
It’s a magnificent, uncompromising performance, crackling with fire and rancid with guilt and nastiness.
Fiennes is terrific as Solness, anchoring himself to the floor in the face of the domestic storm raging around him.

cn.t: Fiennes delivers a magnetic, uncompromising performance that dominates this production of Ibsen's psychologically complex drama about guilt, ambition, and fear of youth. Critics praise the powerful acting and sharp adaptation.
